title: The Electrodyne Engineers and Tesla
summary: How the Sons of Ether remember Tesla's fate.

claims.text: The Electrodyne Engineers, nominally founded in London, drew members across the West while the Order of Reason was turning into the Technocracy.
Tesla impressed the Engineers early and went to the United States to work beside Edison.
Etherites hold that Edison's company claimed credit for Tesla's alternating current work after campaigning against it, and that the Technocracy took what it wanted and then ruined Tesla.

title: Paradigma
summary: The founding text of the Sons of Ether.

claims.text: The Paris presses printed editions of Paradigma, and its loss to sabotage scattered the Tradition's shared language of Science.
A modern team combined surviving editions with a fresh reading of the Kitab al-Alacir to rebuild the fullest record of the Tradition.
Joining means real risk: the Technocracy will try to wreck a new Scientist's public standing, and members are expected to defend one another.

title: Etherite pulp style
summary: Why Sons of Ether dress like heroes from old serials.

claims.text: Other Traditions are puzzled by silver jumpsuits and needless Jacob's Ladders, but for Etherites the look is a deliberate choice.
The pulp style speaks of strong ethics, rugged individuality and a time when bettering humanity was a common dream, a rebuke to Technocratic cynicism.
Freed from the Order of Reason, Ethernauts charted Etherspace and laid the ground for Realms such as the Gernsback Continuum.
Etherspace offered a shortcut for raids on Void Engineer projects, leading to long battles around the Tass-rich Jovian moons that drained both sides.
After the Reckoning closed the way to Etherspace, the Society turned to exploring lost places on Earth and to propulsion for mainstream use.

title: Cybernetic Research Institute
summary: Etherite mechanists, often wrongly called Cybernauts.

claims.text: The Institute was never just about computers, though its close work with the Virtual Adepts through the 1970s and 1980s led many to think so.
Former Electrodyne Engineers formed it in 1910, aiming to share research so the Masses could build their prototypes and so steal assembly-line power from the Union.
They use cybernetic in its older sense, meaning any mechanical control system.

title: The Utopian League
summary: Etherite idealists who shape the Tradition's politics.

claims.text: Proto-psychologists, historians and ethical Scientists formed the League after seeing the Cabal of Pure Thought suppress free energy, travel and health.
Some Cabal members joined them in protest at their own comrades.
A 1905 symposium across Europe set down the Scientific Ethos, with the League charged to ease Etherite work into the Consensus.

title: Adventurers
summary: Cliffhangers, the field Scientists of the Sons of Ether.

claims.text: Adventurers are no formal faction, but every Etherite knows them as Scientists who will not stay in the lab and often save the Tradition.
They publish little, being too busy, so the faction's history is a string of personal tales.
The name was first pinned on Mathieu Hullebusch in 1909 for a flying-automaton bid to overthrow the colonial rulers of the Belgian Congo.

title: Dissidents
summary: The Mad Scientists of the Sons of Ether.

claims.text: Dissidents became a political faction in the First World War, when the Utopian Ethics Council censured or jailed weapon-makers and a minority refused to accept it.
Since the Reckoning they have left self-imposed exile to form small like-minded groups, and the Utopians fear a grab for power.
Dissidents research whatever they please, often one lifelong obsession, and some sell weapons to dictators.
